is_anopheles.evidence: The study examines members of the Anopheles gambiae complex, specifically An. arabiensis, An. merus, and An. quadriannulatus (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions the Vgsc L1014F (kdr) mutation in the context of the SENN DDT laboratory strain (Page 2, Section 2.1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper does not report genotype counts or frequencies for any target markers in the field-collected population. It only states that the SENN DDT laboratory strain is 'fixed for the L1014F kdr mutation' (Page 2, Section 2.1).

african_field_population.evidence: Wild An. arabiensis were collected from Mamfene, Kwazulu-Natal, South Africa (Page 2, Section 2.1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study investigating epigenetic and transcriptomic responses to bacterial stimulation.

sub_country_location.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from Mamfene, Kwazulu-Natal, South Africa (Page 2, Section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Wild specimens were collected between October 2019 and February 2020 (Page 2, Section 2.1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The mosquitoes were collected specifically for this study, though the SENN/SENN DDT/MAFUS/SANGWE laboratory strains are standard colonies.

supplement.evidence: There is no indication that genotype data for the field population is provided in supplementary materials.

assessment.summary: The study investigates the global epigenetic landscape and immune gene expression in Anopheles arabiensis, An. merus, and An. quadriannulatus in response to bacterial stimulation. While it utilizes a laboratory strain (SENN DDT) known to be fixed for the Vgsc L1014F mutation, it does not report any genotype data (counts or frequencies) for the field-collected mosquitoes from South Africa.
exclusion_reasons: No extractable genotype data for the target markers in the field-collected population. The only genotype information provided is for a laboratory strain (SENN DDT).
